Summary:
The provided text is a set of research notes that compile several proposals for reducing unintended side-effects of reinforcement-learning (RL) agents, referencing Armstrong & Levinstein (2017), Amodei et al (2016) and related discussions on reversibility and impact regularisation. The notes sketch four main mechanisms—sentinel-variable penalties, empowerment minimisation, reversibility costs, and a human-feedback normalisation variant—intended to mitigate the risk of agents producing irreversible or harmful environmental changes. 

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[79]  
The guidance produced an integrated fabric linking the single high-level risk through problem analysis, three theoretical insights, two design rationales, four implementation mechanisms, two evidence nodes and four actionable interventions. Every node is connected; no risk–intervention shortcuts remain. The JSON validates against the required schema.  

Inference strategy justification:
The source gives only bullet-level pointers. Moderate inference (confidence 2) was used to (a) phrase risks and problem mechanisms explicitly, and (b) treat cited simulation results and theoretical papers as validation evidence. All inferences are labelled with appropriate confidence scores.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All distinct concepts mentioned (sentinel variables, impact regulariser/empowerment, reversibility cost, human-feedback variant) appear as separate nodes, each linked into the fabric along every required category step. No additional, unreferenced concepts were added.

Key limitations:
1. The notes do not report quantitative results, so validation evidence nodes rely on secondary citation rather than direct data.  
2. Edge confidence is necessarily limited (mostly 2–3).  
3. Section titles were absent; “Bullet list item #” references were used to satisfy traceability requirements.
